proof:
Source. Step 7 of the parent proof (uniqueness, step 2). It supplies the argument behind Simon's statement that |Du| “is uniquely characterized by” (2.4), |Du|(W) = sup{∫ u div g : |g| ≤ 1, spt|g| ⊂ W} (Simon Ch. 2, (2.4), chapter-02.txt lines 518-526): the total variation of the vector measure νμ on an open set is the supremum of its pairings with continuous unit fields supported there. Details written out here.

Let S be the supremum on the right, and call the fields g over which it is taken O-unit fields. Fix a Borel (strongly measurable) ν₀ : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with ν = ν₀ μ-a.e.; this is possible because ν is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Replacing ν by ν₀ changes neither the integrals ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ nor the statement |ν| = 1 μ-a.e.

1. S ≤ μ(O). Let g be an O-unit field. For μ-a.e. x, |⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩| ≤ |g(x)| |ν(x)| = |g(x)| ≤ 1_{tsupport g}(x). Since tsupport g is a compact subset of O, μ(tsupport g) < ∞. So ⟨g, ν⟩, which is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, is μ-integrable, and ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ ≤ μ(tsupport g) ≤ μ(O). Hence ofReal(∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ) ≤ μ(O): this is trivial if μ(O) = ∞, and otherwise ofReal is monotone and ofReal(μ(O)) = μ(O). Taking the supremum, S ≤ μ(O).

2. Reduction to compact sets. O is open in ℝ^N, hence σ-compact: O = ⋃_j K_j with compact K_1 ⊆ K_2 ⊆ …. For example K_j := {x : |x| ≤ j, dist(x, ℝ^N ∖ O) ≥ 1/j}, and K_j := {x : |x| ≤ j} if O = ℝ^N. By continuity of μ from below, μ(O) = sup_j μ(K_j). So it suffices to prove μ(K) ≤ S for every compact K ⊆ O; if K = ∅ there is nothing to prove.

3. Plan. Fix a nonempty compact K ⊆ O and ε > 0; note μ(K) < ∞. We construct an O-unit field g with ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ ≥ μ(K) − 3ε. Then μ(K) ≤ ofReal(∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ) + 3ε ≤ S + 3ε, and letting ε ↓ 0 gives μ(K) ≤ S.

4. A compact neighbourhood L of K. Choose δ₀ > 0 with L₀ := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ δ₀} ⊆ O (K compact, O open; Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). For m ≥ 1 let L_m := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ δ₀/m}. Each L_m is compact, L_m ⊆ L₀ ⊆ O, the L_m decrease in m, and ⋂_m L_m = K because K is closed. Since μ(L₀) < ∞, continuity from above gives μ(L_m ∖ K) → 0. Fix m with μ(L ∖ K) < ε, where L := L_m. The set V := {x : dist(x, K) < δ₀/m} is open and K ⊆ V ⊆ L.

5. Lusin. Let A := K ∩ {x : |ν₀(x)| = 1}, a Borel set with μ(K ∖ A) = 0 and μ(A) ≤ μ(K) < ∞.
- If N = 0, every vector of ℝ^0 has norm 0, so A = ∅ and μ(K) = 0. Then g := 0 gives ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ = 0 ≥ μ(K) − 3ε and we are done.
- Let N ≥ 1. For i = 1, …, N the coordinate ν₀^i is a Borel real function. By Lusin's theorem there is a closed set C_i ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ C_i) < ε/N and ν₀^i continuous on C_i. (This is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, applied to the finite Borel measure μ⌞K on ℝ^N. That measure has the required closed inner regularity because finite Borel measures on metric spaces are weakly regular.)
Put K' := C_1 ∩ … ∩ C_N. Then:
- K' is closed and K' ⊆ A ⊆ K, so K' is compact;
- ν₀ is continuous on K', since all its coordinates are;
- |ν₀| = 1 on K';
- μ(K ∖ K') ≤ μ(K ∖ A) + Σ_i μ(A ∖ C_i) < ε.

6. Tietze. Apply the Tietze extension theorem to each coordinate of ν₀|K' (K' is closed). This gives a continuous G₁ : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with G₁ = ν₀ on K'. Let r(z) := z / max(1, |z|), the radial retraction onto the closed unit ball: it is continuous, |r(z)| ≤ 1, and r(z) = z if |z| ≤ 1. Put G := r ∘ G₁. Then G is continuous, |G| ≤ 1 everywhere, and G = ν₀ on K' because |ν₀| = 1 there.

7. Cut-off. Apply Urysohn's lemma to the compact set K inside the open set V of the locally compact Hausdorff space ℝ^N (Mathlib exists_continuousMap_one_of_isCompact_subset_isOpen). This gives a continuous χ : ℝ^N → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K, tsupport χ compact and tsupport χ ⊆ V. Put g := χ G. Then g is continuous, |g| ≤ 1, and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ V ⊆ L ⊆ O with tsupport g compact. So g is an O-unit field.

8. Estimate. g = 0 outside L. On K', χ = 1 and G = ν₀, so ⟨g, ν₀⟩ = |ν₀|² = 1. On L ∖ K', |⟨g, ν₀⟩| ≤ |g| |ν₀| ≤ 1 μ-a.e. All functions involved are integrable since μ(L) < ∞. Therefore
∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ = ∫⟨g, ν₀⟩ dμ = μ(K') + ∫_{L∖K'} ⟨g, ν₀⟩ dμ ≥ μ(K') − μ(L ∖ K').
Here μ(K') = μ(K) − μ(K ∖ K') > μ(K) − ε, and μ(L ∖ K') = μ(L ∖ K) + μ(K ∖ K') < 2ε. Hence ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ > μ(K) − 3ε, as required in step 3.

9. Conclusion. Steps 2-8 give μ(O) ≤ S, and step 1 gives S ≤ μ(O). Hence μ(O) = S.
key_steps: Every admissible unit field g satisfies ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≤ μ(tsupport g) ≤ μ(O), so the supremum is ≤ μ(O).
μ(O) = sup μ(K) over compact K ⊆ O (σ-compact exhaustion and continuity from below).
For compact K and ε > 0: a compact neighbourhood L ⊆ O with μ(L ∖ K) < ε, and by Lusin a compact K' ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K') < ε on which ν is continuous with |ν| = 1.
Tietze extension, radial retraction and an Urysohn cut-off give a continuous unit field g supported in L with g = ν on K'.
∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≥ μ(K') − μ(L ∖ K') > μ(K) − 3ε, so μ(K) ≤ supremum.
